newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil shares end sharply lower on Wall St-traders.
newsitem.headline: Brazil shares end sharply lower on Wall St-traders.

text.p: Brazilian shares plunged to end down 4.78 percent Friday due to the drop in U.S. stocks and jostling between investors ahead of options expirations on Monday, brokers said.
"It was mostly Wall Street and, of course, options expiration Monday," said John Carioba of local Indusval brokerage.
The Sao Paulo bourse's Bovespa index of 47 most-trade issues closed at 11,334 points on moderate volume of 844.3 million reais ($778 million), according to preliminary bolsa figures.

Brokers said the market tumbled on drops on Wall Street, where the Dow fell 247 points in a market rattled by a weakening dollar, bonds' failure to rally amid benign inflation and worries about blue-chip earnings.
Dealers added the market was hit by speculation and price- jostling by investors with options due to expire on Monday.
"People were pretty nervous all day," Carioba said, adding that drops in benchmark Telebras shook investors holding options with strike prices of 150 reais and 140 reais.
Telebras preferred dropped 5.84 percent to end at 137 reais.
Its common retreated 5.96 percent to close at 123 reais.
While Telebras preferred led the drop among blue chips, other leading shares also plunged.
Federal power holding Eletrobras preferred ended off 5.38 percent to end at 545 reais while mining giant Cia Vale do Rio Doce preferred closed down 4.55 percent at 25.40 reais.
State-owned oil giant Petrobras preferred dropped 5.33 percent to close at 301.01 reais.
The Electrical Energy Index of nine most-liquid power stocks fell 3.03 percent to end at 3,347 points.
Traders said some bank shares bucked the trend, with some state-owned banks jumping in weak trade.
Meanwhile, privately owned Banco Noroeste, which was bought Friday by Spain's Banco Santander, rose 3.36 percent to end at 1.54 reais after having risen as much as nine percent.
